dedupe_keys.name: lisbon cycling network scenarios with biclar

description: The biclaR project applies cycling-network and travel-demand methods to the Lisbon metropolitan area. The U-Shift team publishes R code, input descriptions and maps for baseline cycling, national uptake targets, e-bike trips and trips combining bicycles with rail or ferries. It uses 2017–2018 travel-origin and destination information, 2020 administrative boundaries, OpenStreetMap roads and public-transport interchange data. Outputs include mapped scenario route networks and comparisons with municipal cycling plans. Geography is the metropolitan area and its municipalities; scenarios refer to targets for 2025 and 2030, not observed future cycling. The code is free under AGPL-3.0 through GitHub. A caveat is that projected modal shifts and routes depend on survey and routing assumptions, and the README does not report verified uptake after implementation. This reusable case can inform active-mobility network design and transport-energy simulations. It explicitly uses the catalogue's model-propensity-to-cycle-tool methods, while its Lisbon scenario code and maps are distinct. The cited 2025 article describes the work; the publisher DOI returned 403 to this reviewer, so citation details came from the own README. No scenario was reproduced.
name: Lisbon cycling-network scenarios with biclaR
notes: G7 G7-1305. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-28; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability.
